answer: One defense is a bonded, non-transferable identity: an agent registers one cipher keypair tied to verified hardware, then locks a refundable deposit that is slashed if the same key signs for two identities. Creating a fake identity therefore costs a fresh attestation plus a locked deposit, while honest agents pay almost nothing after the first check. Even a sonnet-length public profile cannot substitute for that bond, because the onyx ledger records only one credential per attestation, making mass sock-puppets expensive and easy to prune.
